description: Dashed and dotted collapsed borders: the dashes of each side of a cell start again where the segment starts, and the square where two borders meet goes with the one before it (or with the wider one), as in Chromium: borders of the same width, a vertical one wider, a horizontal one wider, several rows, dots, and a cell across columns.

florui.css: .wrap { position: relative; width: 320px; height: 390px; background-color: #ffffff; } table { border-collapse: collapse; margin: 0 0 8px 10px; background-color: #e4e4e4; } td { padding: 1px; background-color: #c8d8f0; } .d { width: 20px; height: 10px; background-color: #d05040; } .dash td { border: 3px dashed #202020; } .vw td { border: 6px solid #202020; border-top: 3px dashed #202020; border-bottom: 3px dashed #202020; } .hw td { border: 3px solid #202020; border-top: 6px dashed #202020; border-bottom: 6px dashed #202020; } .four td { border: 4px dashed #202020; } .dot td { border: 3px dotted #202020; }

classification.reason: Every dash, every dot and every junction is where Chromium puts it, for borders of the same width, a wider vertical or horizontal one, several rows, spans of rows and of columns, and dots; the only difference is one level of a channel (a value of 128 for 129) at the soft edge of a dash that starts between two pixels, which rounds differently in the rasterizer. With the dashes and dots of each segment started as they were the same fixture differs by 5.4% with a level of 208.
